newsitem.title: UK: Bradford wool market weak but optimistic.
newsitem.headline: Bradford wool market weak but optimistic.

text.p: Tops prices were largely unchanged in marginally firmer demand but developments in the retail sector brought renewed optimism to the Bradford wool market, trade sources said on Monday.
Selected finer merinos saw slight price improvements and some topmakers had new orders to report, they added.
"After a disappointing September and the sharp price fall for finer merinos in October which made buyers hold back, even (this) modest improvement is encouraging," one said.

Last week's announcement of the 5.2 percent rise in August-September retail clothing prices (the sharpest since 1947) appeared to have little immediate impact on the market as only a limited improvement in buying interest was seen, trade sources said.
Some said the pick-up in retail prices could simply indicate an end to the trend in discounting and the start of the new fashion season.
But others were optimistic that this could still filter down to tops suppliers and bring a willingness from retailers to pay higher prices.
Some sources said that with prices unseasonably weak, buyers could yet take the opportunity to buy forward.

News that a major high street retailer was urging its contracted manufacturers to pay their own suppliers on time also brought cheer to a textile industry where late payment has been endemic, sources said.
